newsitem.title: CHINA: China hopes Albright visit can improve ties.
newsitem.headline: China hopes Albright visit can improve ties.

text.p: China on Tuesday repeated its dismissal of allegations that Beijing may have helped fund U.S. President Bill Clinton's 1996 election campaign and said it hoped upcoming official visits would boost Sino-U.S. ties.

China hoped a visit by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would give Beijing and Washington an opportunity to discuss issues of common interest, Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang told a news briefing.

"We hope this visit to China by Mrs Albright will focus on promoting mutual bilateral understanding and will be beneficial to the betterment and development of relations between the two nations," Tang said.
Chinese Premier Li Peng on Tuesday said Beijing was hoping for continued improvement in relations between the Pacific giants, the official Xinhua news agency said.
"U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Vice President Al Gore will be accorded a cordial reception for their upcoming China visits," Xinhua quoted Li as saying.

Albright is to visit China from February 24-25 and Gore is scheduled to arrive in late March in trips seen by both Beijing and Washington as further steps in mending ties long battered by issues such as human rights, trade and Taiwan.
"The so-called involvement of the Chinese embassy in the United States in raising funds for the Democratic Party of the United States is a complete fabrication," Tang told reporters.
"In handling relations with other nations, China has always seriously observed the principle of mutual non-interference in internal affairs," Tang said, echoing an earlier ministry statement.

The Washington Post reported last week that the Justice Department had found evidence that the Chinese embassy was used for planning contributions to the Democratic National Committee before the 1996 presidential campaign.
Such charges against China were made by people with ulterior motives, Tang said but did not elaborate on what such motives might be.
"We are extremely dissatisfied with such utterly irresponsible reports," he said.
President Bill Clinton has backed a thorough investigation into the allegations, saying he had no knowledge of the charges.
It is illegal for a foreign government or foreigners in most cases to donate to U.S. campaigns.
